_comment: modelWeapon held part 0 only, and part 0 is not the spinner: measured in game space it is a bar 1.096 wide in x, 0.272 tall and 0.182 deep, best-fit axle (0.021, 0.794, -1.500) radius 0.145, sitting at the extreme end of the chassis. That is the AXLE the two punch arms hinge on, not a weapon — the reference photo has the drum in the CENTRE of the machine between the side pods. The drum is part 24: measured x[-0.233,0.224] y[0.456,1.077] z[0.239,0.958], i.e. 0.46 wide across x and 0.62 tall, a cylinder on the x axis dead on the centreline. Part 23 is its hub, x[0.192,0.434] y[0.590,0.973] z[0.382,0.742], centred within 0.04 of the drum's own y and z. Both turn with the rotor; the bracket beside them (part 21, 0.79 wide and offset 0.16 in z from the drum axis) is the fixed bearing block and stays with the chassis.

The arms' axle goes back to the chassis. It is structure: a cylinder turning about its own centreline draws the same picture either way, and leaving it on the rotor is what made the whole bot read as a rear bar spinner.

The drum's spin axle, from rig-inspect --axle over part 24 alone once it was on modelWeapon: game (0.004, 0.740, -0.608), swept radius 0.375, put through --toglb. The hub fits the same axle to within 0.04, and it is left out of the fit because its cone hangs off one side and drags the centre with it.

The arms hinge on the round silver boss at their base, which the axle above runs through, and the partitioner wrote pivotLocal at the FIST end instead ([0, 0.1, -0.05], the far end of a part that spans z -0.070..0.402). This is the axle's best-fit centre (0.021, 0.794, -1.500) in game space put through rig-inspect --toglb.
